script.text: RHINOCEROS
A PLAY IN THREE ACTS
ACT ONE
SCENE ONE: SUMMER IN THE TOWN SQUARE

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The scene is a square in a small provincial town. Upstage a house composed of a ground floor and one story. There is a window of a grocer's shop. The entrance is up two or three steps through a glass-paned door. The word EPICERIE is written in bold letters above the shop window. The two windows on the first floor are the living quarters of the grocer and his wife. The shop is up-stage, but slightly to the left, not far from the wings. In the distance a church steeple is visible above the grocer's house. Between the shop and the left of the stage there is a little street in perspective. To the right is the front of a cafe. The cafe has a terrace, several chairs and tables reach almost to center stage. A dusty tree stands near the terrace chairs. Blue sky; harsh light; very white walls. The time is almost mid day on a Sunday in summer time. JEAN and BERENGER will sit at one of the terrace tables. The sound of church bells is heard, which stop a few moments before the curtain rises. When the curtain rises, a HOUSEWIFE carrying a basket of provisions under one arm and a cat under the other crosses the stage in silence from right to left. As she does so, the GROCER'S WIFE opens her shop door and watches her pass.

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: Oh that woman gets on my nerves! (To her husband who is in the shop) Too stuck-up to buy from us nowadays.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The GROCER's WIFE leaves. JEAN enters right, at the same time as BERENGER enters left. JEAN is very fastidiously dressed: suit, tie, stiff collar, hat. His shoes are yellow and well polished. BERENGER is unshaven and hatless, with unkempt hair and wrinkled clothes. Everything about him indicates negligence. He seems weary, half-asleep; from time to time he yawns..

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (advancing from right) Oh, so you managed to get here at last, Berenger!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (advancing from left) Morning, Jean!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Late as usual, of course. (He looks at his wrist watch.) Our appointment was for 11:30 and now it’s practically midday.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I'm sorry. Have you been waiting long?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: No, I've only just arrived myself, as you saw.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: They go and sit at one of the tables on the cafe terrace.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: In that case I don't feel so bad, if you've only just …

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: It's different with me. I don't like waiting. I'don’t have time to waste. And as you're never on time, I come late on purpose– at a time when I presume you'll be there.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: You're right ... quite right, but …

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Now don't try to pretend you're ever on time!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: No, of course not ... I wouldn't say that.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: JEAN and BERENGER have sat down.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: What are you drinking?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You mean to say you've got a thirst even at this time in the morning?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: It's so hot and dry.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: The more you drink the thirstier you get, popular science tells us that . . .

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: If it would be less dry, we'd be less thirsty.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (studying BERENGER closely) You're not thirsty for water, Berenger...

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I don't understand what you mean.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You know perfectly well what I mean. You're in a bad way, my friend.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: In a bad way? You think so?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: I'm not blind, you know. You’ve gone without your sleep again, you yawn all the time, you’re dead tired…

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: My head feels a bit thick

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You reek of alcohol.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I have got a bit of a hangover, it's true!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: It's the same every Sunday morning– not to mention the other days of the week.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Oh no, it's less frequent during the week, because of the office ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: And what's happened to your tie? Lost it, I suppose.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (puts his hand to his neck) You're right. That's funny! Whatever could I have done with it?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (taking a tie out of his coat pocket) Here, put this one on.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Oh thank you, that is kind. (He puts on the tie.)

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (while BERENGER is unskilfully tying his tie) Your hair's all over the place. Here, here's a comb!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He takes a comb from his other pocket.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (taking the comb) Thank you. (He vaguely combs his hair)

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You haven't even shaved ! Just take a look at yourself!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He takes a mirror from his inside pocket, hands it to BERENGER, who looks at himself as he does so, he examines his tongue.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: My tongue's all coated.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: taking the mirror, then the comb and putting it back in his pocket

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: I'm not surprised! You're heading for cirrhosis, my friend.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (worried) Do you think so?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER, who wants to give him back his tie) Keep the tie, I've got plenty more.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (admiringly) You always look so immaculate.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (continuing his inspection of BERENGER) Your clothes are all crumpled, they're a disgrace! Your shirt is downright filthy, and your shoes ...

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: BERENGER tries to hide his feet under the table.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: What a mess you're in! And look at your shoulders ...

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: What's the matter with my shoulders?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Turn around! Come on, turn around ! You've been leaning against some wall. (BERENGER holds his hand out docilely to JEAN.) No, I haven't got a brush with me; it would make my pockets bulge.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: Still docile, BERENGER flicks his shoulders to get rid of the white dust; JEAN averts his head. Heavens! Where did you get all that from?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: You're very hard on me ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: I've every reason to be.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Listen, Jean. There are so few distractions in this town-I get so bored. I'm not made for the work I'm doing… every day at the office, eight hours a day-and only three weeks holiday a year!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: When Saturday night comes round I feel exhausted and so–you know how it is–just to relax ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: My dear man, everybody has to work. I spend eight hours a day in the office the same as everyone else. And I only get three weeks off a year, but even so. you don't catch me … Willpower, my good man!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: But everybody hasn't got as much willpower as you have. I can't get used to it. I just can't get used to life.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Everybody has to get used to it .. Or do you consider yourself some superior being?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I don't pretend to be ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (interrupting him) I'm just as good as you are; I think with all due modesty I may say I'm better.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The superior man is the man who fulfils his duty.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: What duty?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: His duty ... His duty as an employee, for example.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Oh yes, his duty as an employee ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Where did your debauchery take place last night? If you can remember!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: We were celebrating Auguste's birthday, our friend Auguste ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Our friend Auguste? Nobody invited me to our friend Auguste's birthday . . . At this moment a noise is heard, far off, but swiftly approaching, of a beast panting in its headlong course, and of a long trumpeting.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I couldn't refuse. It wouldn't have been nice ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Did I go there?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Well, perhaps it was because you weren't invited.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: (coming out of cafe) Good morning, gentlemen. Can l get you something to drink?

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The noise becomes very loud.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER, almost shouting to make himself heard above the noise which he has not become conscious of) True, I was not invited. That honour was denied me.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: But in any case, I can assure you that even if I had been invited, I would not have gone, because… (The noise has become intense.) What's going on?

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The noise of a powerful, heavy animal, galloping at great speed is heard very close; the sound of panting.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Whatever is it?

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: Whatever is it?

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: BERENGER, still listless without appearing to hear anything at all, replies tranquilly to JEAN about the invitation; his lips move but one doesn't hear what he says. JEAN bounds to his feet, knocking his chair over as he does so, looks off left pointing, whilst BERENGER, still a little dopey, remains seated.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Oh, a rhinoceros! The noise made by the animal dies away swiftly and one can already hear the following words.-The whole of this scene must be played very fast, each repeating in swift succession: 'Oh, a rhinoceros!'

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: Oh, a rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (sticks her head out of her shop doorway) Oh, a rhinoceros! (To her husband still inside the shop) Quick, come and look; it's a rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: They are all looking off after the animal.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: It's rushing straight ahead, brushing up against the shop windows.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (in his shop) Whereabouts?

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: (putting her hands on her hips) Well!

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (to her husband who is still in shop) Come and look!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: At this moment the GROCER puts his head out.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: Oh, a rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (entering quickly left) A rhinoceros going full-tilt on the opposite pavement!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: All these speeches from the time when JEAN says 'Oh, a rhinoceros' are practically simultaneous. A woman is heard crying 'Ah!' She appears. She runs to the center stage; it is a HOUSEWIFE with a basket on her arm; once arrived centre-stage she drops her basket; the contents scatter all over the stage, a bottle breaks, but she does not drop her cat.

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: Ah! Oh!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: An elegant OLD GENTLEMAN comes from left stage, after the HOUSEWIFE, rushes into the GROCER'S shop, knocks into the GROCER and his WIFE, whilst the LOGICIAN installs himself against the back wall on the left of the grocery entrance. JEAN and the WAITER, standing, and BERENGER, still apathetically seated, together form another group. At the same time, coming from the left, cries of 'Oh' and 'Ah' and the noise of people running have been heard. The dust raised by the animal spreads over the stage.

script.speaker: Cafe Proprietor
script.text: (sticking his head out of the first-floor window) What's going on?

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (disappearing behind the GROCER and his WIFE) Excuse me, please!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The OLD GENTLEMAN is elegantly dressed, with white spats, a soft hat and an ivory-handled cane; the LOGICIAN, propped up against the wall has a little grey moustache, an eyeglass, and is wearing a straw hat.

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Watch out with that stick!

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: Look where you're going, can't you!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The head of the OLD GENTLEMAN is seen behind the GROCER and his WIFE.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: (to the PROPRIETOR) A rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the WAITER) You're seeing things. (He sees the rhinoceros) Well, I'll be . . . !

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: Ah! The 'Ohs' and 'Ahs' from off-stage form a background accompaniment to her 'Ah'. She has dropped her basket, her provisions and the bottle, but has nevertheless kept tight hold of her cat which she carries under her other arm.

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: There, they frightened the poor kitty!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: PROPRIETOR is still looking off left following the distant course of the animal as the noises fade; hooves, trumpetings, etc. BERENGER sleepily averts his head a little on account of the dust, but says nothing; he simply makes a grimace.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: Well, of all things!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: also averting his head a little, but very much awake

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Well, of all things! (He sneezes.)

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: she is center stage her things scattered on the ground round her

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: Well of all things!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: She sneezes. The OLD GENTLEMAN, GROCER'S WIFE and GROCER up-stage re-opening the glass door of the GROCER'S shop that the OLD GENTLEMAN has closed behind him.

script.speaker: All Three
script.text: Well, of all things !

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Well, of all things! (To BERENGER) Did you see that? The noise of the rhinoceros and its trumpeting are now far away; the people are still staring after the animal, all except for BERENGER who is still apathetically seated.

script.speaker: All
script.text: (except BERENGER) ) Well, of all things!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) It certainly looked as if it was a rhinoceros. It made plenty of dust.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He takes out a handkerchief and blows his nose.

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: Well, of all things! Gave me such a scare.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Your basket ... and all your things ...

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The OLD GENTLEMAN approaches the lady and bends to pick up her things scattered about the stage. He greets her gallantly, raising his hat.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: Really, these days, you never know ...

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: Fancy that!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) May I help you pick up your things?

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Thank you, how very kind! Do put on your hat. Oh, it gave me such a scare!

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: Fear is an irrational thing. It must yield to reason.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: It's already out of sight.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE and indicating the LOGICIAN) My friend is a logician.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Well, what did you think of that?

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: Those animals can certainly travel!

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) Very happy to meet you!

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (to the GROCER) That'll teach her to buy her things from somebody else!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to the PROPRIETOR and the WAITER) What did you think of that?

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: I still didn't let my cat go.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (shrugging his shoulders, at window) You don't often see that!

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN and the OLD GENTLEMAN who is picking up her groceries) Would you hold him a moment!

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: (to JEAN) First time I've seen that!

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE, taking the cat in his arms) It's not spiteful, is it?

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to JEAN) Went past like a comet!

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) He wouldn't hurt a fly. (To the others:) What happened to my wine?

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) I've got plenty more.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Well, what did you think of that?

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) And good stuff, too!

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the WAITER) Don't hang about! Look after these gentlemen! (He indicates

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: BERENGER and JEAN. He exits.)

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) What did I think of what?

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (to the GROCER) Go·and get her another bottle!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Of the rhinoceros, of course! What did you think I meant?

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) I've got some first class wine, in unbreakable bottles! (He disappears into his shop.)

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (stroking the cat in his arms) Kitty, kitty, kitty.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: (to BERENGER and JEAN) What are you drinking?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Two pastis.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: Two pastis-right! (He walks to the cafe entrance.)

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: picking up her things with the help of the OLD GENTLEMAN

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: Very kind of you, I'm sure.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: Two pastis! (She goes into cafe.)

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Oh, please don't mention it, it's a pleasure.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The GROCER'S WIFE goes into shop.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN and the HOUSEWIFE picking up the provisions) Replace them in an orderly fashion.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Well, What did you think about it?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN, not knowing what to say) Well ... nothing . . . it made a lot of dust ...

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: coming out of shop with a bottle of wine, to the HOUSEWIFE

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: I've got some good leeks as well.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (still stroking the cat) Kitty, Kitty, Kitty. of France. It is characterized by its licorice and star anise flavor, usually served diluted with water, which causes it to turn a cloudy, pale yellow.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) It's a hundred francs a litre.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: paying the GROCER, then to the OLD GENTLEMAN who has managed to put everything back in the basket

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: Oh, you are kind! Such a pleasure to come across the old French courtesy. Not like the young people today!

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (taking money) You should buy from me. You wouldn't even have to cross the street, and you wouldn't run the risk of these accidents. (He goes back into his shop.)

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: who has sat down and is still thinking of the rhinoceros

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: But you must admit it's extraordinary.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: taking off his hat, and kissing the HOUSEWIFE’S hand

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: It was a great pleasure to meet you!

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) Thank you very much for holding my cat.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The LOGICIAN gives the HOUSEWIFE back her cat. The WAITER comes back with drinks.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: Two pastis!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) You're incorrigible!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) May I accompany you part of the way?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN, and pointing to the WAITER who goes back into the cafe.) I asked for mineral water. He's made a mistake.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: JEAN, scornful and disbelieving, shrugs his shoulders.

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) My husband's waiting for me, thank you. Perhaps some other time …

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) I sincerely hope so ,Madame.

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) So do I!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: She gives him a sweet look as she leaves left.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: The dust's settled ...

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: JEAN shrugs his shoulders again.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN, looking after the HOUSEWIFE) Delightful creature!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) A rhinoceros! I can't get over it!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The OLD GENTLEMAN and the LOGICIAN move slowly right and off. They chat amiably.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN, after looking fondly at the HOUSEWIFE) Charming, isn't she? 7 Incorrigible: incapable of being corrected or amended. Unruly.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) I'm going to explain to you what a syllogism is.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Ah yes, a syllogism.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) I can't get over it! It's unthinkable! (BERENGER yawns.)

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: A syllogism consists of a main proposition, a secondary one, and a conclusion.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: What conclusion?

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The LOGICIAN and the OLD GENTLEMAN go out.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: I just can't get over it..

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Yes, I can see you can't. Well, it was a rhinoceros– all right, so it was a rhinoceros! It's miles away by now ... miles away ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: But you must see it's fantastic ! A rhinoceros loose in the town, and you don't bat an eyelid! It shouldn't be allowed!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: BERENGER yawns.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Put your hand in front of your mouth!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Yes ... yes ... It shouldn't be allowed. It's dangerous. I hadn't realized. But don't worry about it, it won't get us here.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: We ought to protest to the Town Council! What's the Council there for?

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: yawning, then quickly putting his hand to his mouth

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Oh excuse me ... perhaps the rhinoceros escaped from the zoo.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You're day-dreaming.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: But I'm wide awake.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: There's no difference between dreaming awake and dreaming asleep. You're certainly dreaming when you say the rhinoceros escaped from the zoo ...

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I only said perhaps.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: ... because there's been no zoo in our town since the animals were destroyed in the plague ... ages ago ... two given propositions (or premises) . If the initial statements are true, the conclusion must inevitably be true

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (with the same indifference) Then perhaps it came from a circus.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: What circus are you talking about?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I don't know ... some travelling circus.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You know perfectly well that the Council banned all travelling performers from the district ... There haven't been any since we were children.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (trying unsuccessfully to stop yawning) In that case, maybe it's been hiding ever since in the surrounding swamps?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: The surrounding swamps! The surrounding swamps! My poor friend, you live in a thick haze of alcohol. It's clouding your brain! Where do you know of any surrounding swamps? Our county is known as 'little Spain' because the land is so arid.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (surfeited and pretty weary) How do I know, then? Perhaps it's been hiding under a stone? ... Or maybe it's been nesting on some withered branch?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: If you think you're being witty, you're very much mistaken ! You're incapable of talking seriously!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Today, yes, only today...because of…because of... (He indicates his head with a vague gesture.)

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Today is the same as any other day!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Oh, not quite as much.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Your witticisms are not very inspired.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I wasn't trying to be ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (interrupting him) I can't bear people who try to make fun of me!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (hand on his heart) But my dear Jean, I'd never allow myself to …

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (interrupting him) My dear Berenger, you are allowing yourself …

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Oh no, never, I'd never allow myself to.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Yes, you· would; you've just done so.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: But how could you possibly think ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (interrupting him) I think what is true!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: But I assure you …

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (interrupting him) ... that you were making fun of me!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: You really can be obstinate10, sometimes.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: And now you're calling me a mule. Even you must see how insulting you're being.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: It would never have entered my mind.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You have no mind!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: All the more reason why it would never enter it.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: There are certain things which enter the minds of even people without one.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: That's impossible.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: And why, pray, is it impossible?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Because it's impossible.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Then kindly explain to me why it's impossible, as you seem to imagine you can explain everything.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I don't imagine anything of the kind.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Then why do you act as if you do? And, I repeat, why are you being so insulting to me?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I'm not insulting you. Far from it. You know what tremendous respect I have for you.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: In that case, why do you contradict me, making out that it's not dangerous to let a rhinoceros go racing about in the middle of the town, particularly on a Sunday morning when the streets are full of children... and adults, too...

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: A lot of them are in church. They don't run any risk...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (interrupting him) If you will allow me to finish·... and at market time, too.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I never said it wasn't dangerous to let a rhinoceros go racing about the town. I simply said I'd personally never considered the danger. It had never crossed my mind.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You never consider anything.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: All right, I agree. A rhinoceros roaming about is not a good thing. to persuade them otherwise

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: It shouldn't be allowed.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I agree. It shouldn't be allowed. It's a ridiculous thing all right! But it's no reason for you and me to argue. Why go on at me just because some wretched perissodactyl11 happens to pass by?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: A stupid quadruped not worth talking about, which has already disappeared, and therefore doesn't exist any longer. Why should we bother about some animal that doesn't exist? Let's talk about some-thing else, Jean, please; (He yawns.)

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: There are plenty of other subjects for conversation. (He takes his glass) To you!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: At this moment the LOGICIAN and the OLD GENTLEMAN come back on stage from left; they walk over, talking as they go, to one of the tables on the cafe terrace, some distance from BERENGER and JEAN, behind and to the right of them.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Put that glass back on the table! You're not to drink it.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: JEAN takes a large swallow from his own pastis and puts back the glass, half-empty, on the table. BERENGER continues to hold his glass without putting it down, and without daring to drink from it either.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (timidly) There's no point in leaving it for the proprietor. (He makes as if to drink.)

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Put it down, I tell you!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Very well.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He is putting the glass back on the table when DAISY passes. She is a young typist and she crosses the stage from right to left; When he sees her, BERENGER rises abruptly, and in doing so makes an awkward movement; the glass falls and splashes JEAN's trousers.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Oh, there's Daisy!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Look out! How clumsy you are!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: That's Daisy... I'm so sorry... (He hides himself out of sight of DAISY.) I don't want her to see me in this state.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Your behaviour's unforgivable, absolutely unforgivable!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He looks in the direction of DAISY, who is just disappearing.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Why are you afraid of that young girl?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Oh, be quiet, please be quiet!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: She doesn't look like an unpleasant person!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: coming back to JEAN, now that DAISY has gone

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I must apologize once more for ... middle (third) toe of each foot

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You see what comes of drinking? You can no longer control your movements. You're digging your own grave, my friend, you're destroying yourself.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I don't like the taste of alcohol much. And yet if I don't drink, I'm done for. It's as if I'm frightened, and so I drink not to be frightened any longer.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Frightened of what?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I don't know exactly. It's a sort of anguish difficult to describe. I feel out of place in life, among people, and so I take to drink. That calms me down and relaxes me so I can forget.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You try to escape from yourself!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I'm so tired, I've been tired for years. I'm conscious of my body all the time, as if it were made of lead, or as if I were carrying another man around on my back. I can't seem to get used to myself. I don't even know if I am me.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Then as soon as I take a drink, the lead slips away and I recognize myself, I become me again.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: That's just being fanciful. Look at me, Berenger, I weigh more than you do. And yet I feel light, light as a feather!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: JEAN flaps his arms as if about to fly. The OLD GENTLEMAN and the LOGICIAN have come back and have taken a few steps on stage deep in talk. At this moment they are passing by JEAN and BERENGER. JEAN'S arm deals the OLD GENTLEMAN a sharp knock which precipitates him into the arms of the LOGICIAN.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: An example of a syllogism ... (He is knocked.) Oh!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to JEAN) Look out ! (To the LOGICIAN) I'm so sorry.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) I'm so sorry.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) No harm done.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to JEAN) No harm done.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The OLD GENTLEMAN and the LOGICIAN go and sit at one of the terrace tables a little to the right and behind JEAN and BERENGER.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) You certainly are strong.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Yes, I'm strong. I'm strong for several reasons. In the first place I'm strong because I'm naturally strong, and·secondly I'm strong because ·I have moral strength. I'm also strong because I'm not riddled with alcohol.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: I don't wish to offend you, my dear Berenger, but I feel I must tell you that it's alcohol which weighs so heavy on you.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Here is an example of a syllogism. The cat has four paws. Isidore and Fricot both have four paws. Therefore Isidore and Fricot are cats.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) My dog has got four paws.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Then it's a cat.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) I've barely got the strength to go on living. Maybe I don't even want to.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN, after deep reflection) So then logically speaking, my dog must be a cat?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Logically, yes. But the contrary is also true.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) Solitude seems to oppress me. And so does the company of other people.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) You contradict yourself. What oppresses you, solitude, or the company of others? You consider your... self a thinker, yet you're devoid of logic. .

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) Logic is a very beautiful thing.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) As long as it is not abused.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) Life is an abnormal business.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: On the contrary. Nothing could be more natural, and the proof is that people go on living.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: There are more dead people than living. And their numbers are increasing. The living are getting rarer.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: The dead don't exist, there's no getting away from that! ... Ah!….ah! (He gives a huge laugh.) Yet you're oppressed by them, too? How can you be oppressed by something that doesn't exist?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I sometimes wonder if l exist myself

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You don't exist, my dear Berenger, because you don't think. Start thinking, then you will.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Another syllogism. All cats, die. Socrates is dead. Therefore Socrates is a cat.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: And he's got four paws. That's true. I've got a cat named Socrates.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: There you are, you see ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Fundamentally you're just a bluffer. And a liar. You say that life doesn't interest you. And yet there's somebody who does.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Who?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Your little friend from the office who just went past. You're very fond of her!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) So Socrates was a cat, was he?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: Logic has just revealed the fact to us.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) You didn't want her to see you in your present state. (BERENGER makes a gesture.) That proves you're not indifferent to everything. But how can you expect Daisy to be attracted to a drunkard?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Let's get back to our cats.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) I'm all ears.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) In any case, I think she's already got her eye on someone.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Oh, who?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Dudard. An office colleague, qualified in law, with a big future in the firm-and in Daisy's affections. I can't hope to compete with him.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) The cat Isidore has four paws.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: How do you know?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: It's stated in the hypothesis.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) The Chief thinks a lot of him. Whereas I've no future, I've no qualifications. I don't stand a chance.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) Ah! in the hypothesis.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) So you're giving up, just like that ... ?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: What else can I do?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to OLD GENTLEMAN) Fricot also has four paws. So how many paws have Fricot and Isidore?

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Separately or together?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Life is a struggle, it's cowardly not to put up a fight!

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Separately or together, it all depends.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) What can I do? I've nothing to put up a fight with.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Then find yourself some weapons, my friend.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN,· after painful reflection) Eight, eight paws.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: Logic involves mental arithmetic, you see.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: It certainly has many aspects!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) Where can I find the weapons?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) There are no limits to logic.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Within yourself. Through your own will.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: What weapons?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) I'm going to show you ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) The weapons of patience and culture, the weapons of the mind. (BERENGER yawns.) Turn yourself into a keen and brilliant intellect. Get yourself up to the mark!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: How do I get myself up to the mark?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the-OLD GENTLEMAN) If l take two paws away from these cats-how many does each have left?

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: That's not so easy.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) That's not so easy.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) On the contrary, it's simple.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) It may be simple for you, but not for me.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) It may be·simple for you, but not for me..

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Come on, exercise your mind. Concentrate!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Come on, exercise your will. Concentrate!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) I don't see how.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) I really don't see how.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) You have to be told everything.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) You have to be told everything.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Take a sheet of paper and calculate. If you take six paws from the two cats, how many paws are left to each cat?

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Just a moment...

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He calculates on a sheet of paper which he takes from his pocket.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: This is what you must do: dress yourself properly, shave every day, put on a clean shirt.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: The laundry's so expensive …

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Cut down on your drinking. This is the way to come out: wear a hat, a tie like this, a well-cut suit, shoes well polished

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: As he mentions. the various items of clothing he points self contentedly to his own hat, tie and shoes.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) There are several possible solutions.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Tell me.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) Then what do I do? Tell me ...

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) I'm listening.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: ((to JEAN) I'm listening.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You're a timid creature, but not without talent.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I've got talent, me?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: So use it. Put yourself in the picture. Keep abreast of the cultural and literary events of the times.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) One possibility is: one cat could have four paws and the other two.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) I get so little spare time!

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) You're not without talent. You just needed to exercise it.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Take advantage of what free time you do have. Don't just let yourself drift.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: I've never had the time. I was an official, you know.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: One can always find time to learn.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) One can always find time.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) It's too late now.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) It's a bit late in the day for me.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) It's never too late.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) It's never too late.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) You work eight hours a day, like me and everybody else, but not on Sundays, nor in the evening, nor for three weeks in the summer. That's quite sufficient, with a little method.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Well, what about the other solutions? Use a little method, a little method!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The OLD GENTLEMAN starts to calculate anew.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Look, instead of drinking and feeling sick, isn't it better to be fresh and eager, even at work? And you can spend your free time constructively.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: How do you mean?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: By visiting museums, reading literary periodicals, going to lectures. That'll solve your troubles, it will develop your mind. In four weeks you'll be a cultured man.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: You're right!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) There could be one cat with five paws ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) You see, you even think so yourself!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) And one cat with one paw. But would they still be cats, then?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Why not?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Instead of squandering all your spare money or drink, isn't it better to bμy a ticket for an interesting play? Do you know anything about the avant-garde theater there's so much talk about? Have you seen Ionesco's plays?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) Unfortunately, no. I've only heard people talk about them.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) By taking two of the eight paws away from the two cats ...

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) There's one playing now. Take advantage of it.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) ... we could have one cat with six paws ...

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: It would be an excellent initiation into the artistic life of our times.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) We could have one cat with no paws at all.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: You're right, perfectly right. I'm going to put myself into the picture, like you said.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) In that case, one cat would be specially privileged.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) I will, I promise you.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You promise yourself, that's the main thing.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: And one under-privileged cat deprived of all paws.·

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I make myself a solemn promise, I'll keep my word to myself.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: That would be unjust, and therefore not logical.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Instead of drinking, I'll develop my mind. I feel better already. My head already feels clearer.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: You see!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) Not logical?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: This afternoon I'll go to the museum. And I'll book two seats for the theatre this evening. Will you come with me?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Because Logic means Justice.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) You must persevere. Keep up your good resolutions.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) I get it. Justice; ..

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) I promise you, and I promise myself. Will you come to the museum with me this afternoon?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) I have to take a rest this afternoon; it's in my programme for the day.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Justice is one more aspect of Logic.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) But you will come with me to the theatre this evening?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: No, not this evening.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: LOGICIAN·: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Your mind is getting clearer!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) I sincerely hope you'll keep up your good resolutions. But this evening I have to meet some friends for a drink.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: For a drink?

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) What's more, a cat with no paws at all …

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) I've promised to go. I always keep my word.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the LOGICIAN) ... wouldn't be able to run fast enough to catch mice.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) Ah, now it's you that's setting me a bad example ! You're going out drinking.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) You're already making progress in logic.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: A sound of rapid galloping is heard approaching again, trumpeting and the sound of rhinoceros hooves and pantings; this time the sound comes from the opposite direction approaching from back-stage to front, in the left wings.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (furiously to BERENGER) It's not a habit with me, you know. It's not the same as with you. With you ... you're… it's not the same thing at all …

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Why isn't it the same thing?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (shouting over the noise coming from the cafe) I'm no drunkard, not me!

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (shouting to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Even with no paws a cat must catch mice. That's in it's nature.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (shouting very loudly) I didn't mean you were a drunkard. But why would it make me one any more than you, in a case like.that?

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (shouting to the LOGICIAN) What's in the cat's nature?·

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Because there's moderation in all things. I'm a moderate person, not like you!

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to the. OLD GENTLEMAN, cupping his hands to his ears) What did you say? Deafening sounds drown the words of the four characters.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN, cupping his hands to his ears) What about me, what? What did you say?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (roaring) I said that ...

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (roaring) I said that ...

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: suddenly aware of the noises which are now very near

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: What ever's happening?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: What is going on?

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: rises, knocking his chair over as he does so; looks towards left wings where the noises of the passing rhinoceros are coming from

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Oh, a rhinoceros !

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (rising, knocking over his chair) Oh, a rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (doing the same) Oh, a rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (still seated, but this time, taking more notice) Rhinoceros! In the opposite direction!

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: (emerging with a tray and glasses) What is it? Oh, a rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He drops the tray, breaking the glasses.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (coming out of the cafe) What's going on?

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: (to the PROPRIETOR) A rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: A rhinoceros, going full-tilt on the opposite pave-ment!

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (coming out of his shop) Oh, a rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Oh, a rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: sticking her head through the upstairs window of shop

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: Oh, a rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: It's no reason to break the glasses.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: It's rushing straight ahead, brushing up against the shop windows.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: (entering left) Oh, a rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (noticing DAISY) Oh, Daisy! Noise of people fleeing, the same 'Ohs' and 'Ahs' as before.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: Well, of all things !

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the WAITER) You’ll be charged up for those!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: BERENGER tries to make himself scarce, not to be seen by DAISY. The OLD GENTLEMAN, the LOGICIAN, the GROCER and his WIFE move to centre-stage and say together.

script.speaker: All
script.text: Well, of all things!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: JEAN & BERENGER: Well, of all things! A piteous meowing is heard, then an equally pitous cry of a woman.

script.speaker: All
script.text: Oh!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: Almost at the same time, and as the noises are rapidly dying away the HOUSEWIFE appears without her basket but holding the blood-stained corpse of her cat in her arms.

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (wailing) It ran over my cat, it ran over my cat!

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: It ran over her cat!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The GROCER, his WIFE (at the window),the OLD GENTLEMAN, DAISY and the LOGICIAN crowd round the HOUSEWIFE, saying:

script.speaker: All
script.text: What a tragedy, poor little thing!

script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE; from window) Don't upset yourself!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Don't upset yourself, dear lady!

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (from window) It's very upsetting a thing like that!

script.speaker: Housewife

script.speaker: Proprietor

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: HOUSEWIFE at one of the terrace tables, still cradling her dead cat.) A glass of water for the lady.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Poor woman!

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (from window) Poor cat!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to the WAITER) Better give her a brandy.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the WAITER) A brandy! (Pointing to BERENGER:) This gentleman is paying!

script.text: (going into the cafe) One brandy, right away!

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (sobbing) I don't want any, I don't want any!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to the GROCER) It wasn't the same one!

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (to JEAN) But I could have …

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: Yes it was, it was the·same one.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: Did it go past twice, then?

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: I think it was the same one.

script.speaker: Jean

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The WAITER appears with a glass of brandy and takes it to the HOUSEWIFE.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (in tears) No ...o ...o …

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (suddenly unnerved, to JEAN) You're talking non-sense ... How could you possibly tell about the horns? The animal flashed past at such speed, we hardly even saw it.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Go on, it will do you good!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to BERENGER) Very true. It did go fast.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Just have a taste, it's good.

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (to the WAITER, from window) Make her drink it.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) What's more, it was travelling in a cloud of dust.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Drink it up.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Just a sip, dear little lady be brave ...

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The WAITER forces her to drink it by putting the glass to her lips; the HOUSEWIFE feigns refusal, but drinks all the same.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: There, you see!

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (from her window) and DAISY: There, you see!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) I don't have to·grope my way through a fog. I can calculate quickly, my mind is clear!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Better now?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) But it had its head thrust down.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Now wasn't that good?

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Precisely, one could see all the better.

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (after having drunk) My little cat!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (irritated) Utter nonsense!

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE, from window) I've got another cat you can have.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) What me? You dare to accuse me of talking nonsense?

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (to the GROCER'S WIFE) I'll never have another! (She weeps, cradling her cat.)

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) Yes, absolute, blithering nonsense!

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) You have to accept these things!

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) I've never talked nonsense in my life!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Try and be philosophic about it!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) You're just a pretentious show-off (Raising his voice) A pedant!

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to JEAN and BERENGER) Now, gentlemen!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN, continuing) ... and what's more, a pedant who's not certain of his facts because in the first place it's the Asian rhinoceros with only one horn on its nose, and it's the African with two…

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The other characters leave the HOUSEWIFE and crowd around JEAN and BERENGER who argue at the top of their voices.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) You're wrong, it's the other way about!

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (left alone) He was so sweet!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Do you want to bet?

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: They want to make a bet!

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: (to BERENGER) Don't excite yourself, Mr. Berenger.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) I'm not betting with you. If anybody's got two horns, it's you! You beast!

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: Oh!

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (from window to her husband) They're going to have a fight!

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (to his WIFE) Nonsense, it's just a bet!

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to JEAN and BERENGER) We don't want any scenes here!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Now look ... What kind of rhinoceros has one horn on its nose? (To the

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: ) You're a tradesman, you should know.

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (to her husband) Yes, you should know!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) I've got no horns. And I never will have.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) Tradesmen can't be expected to know everything.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) Oh yes, you have!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) I'm not Asian either.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: There’s nothing wrong with being Asian .

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: It was an African Rhinoceros.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the PROPRIETOR) That's true!

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the WAITER) Nobody's asking for your opinion!

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: (to the PROPRIETOR) She's right.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The HOUSEWIFE continues to lament throughout this discussion

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: He was so gentle, just like one of us.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The LOGICIAN, a little to one side between the HOUSEWIFE and the group which has formed round JEAN and BERENGER, follows the controversy attentively, without taking part.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: Goodbye gentlemen! (To BERENGER:) You, I will not deign12 to include!

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: He was devoted to us! (She sobs.)

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: Now listen a moment, Mr. Berenger, and you, too, Mr. Jean…

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: I once had some friends who were Asian!

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (still sobbing) I had him when he was a little kitten.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (still quite beside himself) It was AFRICAN!

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) Whatever it was, you’re the one acting like a horned beast.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: GROCERS WIFE (from window) and WAITER: Oh!

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: This is getting serious!

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: He was so clean. He always used his litter box.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) If that's how you feel, it's the last time you'll see me. I'm not wasting my time with a fool like you.

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: He always made himself understood.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: JEAN goes off right, very fast and furious ... but doubles back before making his final exit.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the GROCER) There are rhinoceroses with two horns, some with one horn, and there are other rhinoceroses with no horns, like us.

script.speaker: Jean
script.text: (to BERENGER) You drunkard! Everybody looks at him in consternation.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to JEAN) I'm not going to stand for that!

script.speaker: All
script.text: (looking in JEAN'S direction) Oh!

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: He could almost talk–in fact, he did.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: (to BERENGER) You shouldn't have made him angry.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to DAISY) It wasn't my fault.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the WAITER) Go and get a little coffin for the poor thing …

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to BERENGER) I think you're right. It's the Asian rhinoceros with two horns and the African with one …

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: But he was saying the opposite.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: (to BERENGER) You were both wrong!

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to BERENGER) Even so, you were right.

script.speaker: Waiter
script.text: (to the HOUSEWIFE) Come with me, we're going to put him in a little box.

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (sobbing desperately) No, never!

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: If you don't mind my saying so, I think Mr. Jean was right.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: (Turning to the HOUSEWIFE) Now, you must be reasonable!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: DAISY and the WAITER lead the HOUSEWIFE, with her dead cat, towards the cafe entrance.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to DAISY and the WAITER) Would you like me to come with you?

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: The Asian rhinoceros has one horn and the African rhinoceros has two. And vice versa.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) No, don't you bother.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: DAISY and the WAITER enter the cafe leading the inconsolable HOUSEWIFE.

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (to the GROCER, from window) Oh you always have to be different from everybody else!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: aside, whilst the others continue to discuss the horns of the rhinoceros

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Daisy was right, I should never have contradicted him.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the GROCER'S WIFE) Your husband's right, the Asian rhinoceros has two horns and the African one must have two, and vice versa.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (aside) He can't stand being contradicted. The slightest disagreement makes him fume

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to the PROPRIETOR) You're mistaken, my friend.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the OLD GENTLEMAN) I'm very sorry, I'm sure.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (aside) His temper's his only fault..

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: from window, to the OLD GENTLEMAN, the PROPRIETOR and the GROCER

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: Maybe they're both the same..'

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (aside) Deep down, he's got a heart of gold; he's done me many a good tμrn.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (to the GROCER'S WIFE) If the one has two horn, then the other must have one.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Perhaps it's the other with two and the one with one.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (aside) I'm sorry I wasn't more accommodating. But why is he so obstinate13? (To the others) He's always making fantastic statements! Always trying to dazzle people with his knowledge. He never will admit he's wrong.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to BERENGER) Have you any proof?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Proof of what?

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Of the statement you made just now which started the unfortunate row with your friend.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (to BERENGER) Yes, have you any proof? .

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to BERENGER) How do you know that one of the two rhinoceroses has one horn and the other two? And which is which?

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: He doesn't know any more than we do.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: In the first place we don't know that there were two. I myself believe there was only one.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: Well, let's say there were two. Does the single-horned one come from Asia?

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: No. It's the one from Africa with two, I think.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: Which is two-horned?

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: It's not the one from Africa.

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: It's not easy to agree·on this.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: But the problem must be cleared up.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (emerging from his isolation) Excuse me gentlemen for interrupting. But that is not the question. Allow me to introduce myself …

script.speaker: Housewife
script.text: (coming out of the cafe in tears) He's a logician.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: Oh! A logician, is he?

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (introducing the LOGICIAN to BERENGER) My friend, the Logician.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Very happy to meet you.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (continuing) Professional Logician; my card. (He shows his card.) change.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: It's a great honour.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: A great honour for all of us.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: Would you mind telling us then, sir, if the African rhinoceros is single-horned .. .

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Or bicorned .. .

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: And is the Asian rhinoceros bicorned ...

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: Or unicorned.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: Exactly, that: is not the question. Let me make myself clear.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: But it's still what we want to find out.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: Kindly allow me to speak, gentlemen.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Let him speak! .

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (to the GROCER, from window) Give him a chance to speak.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: We're listening, sir.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to BERENGER) I'm addressing you in particular. And all the others present as well.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: Us as well ...

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: You see, you have got away from the problem which instigated the debate. In the first place you were deliberating whether or not the rhinoceros which passed by just now was the same one that passed by earlier, or whether it was another.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: That is the question to decide.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Yes, but how?

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: Thus: you may have seen on two occasions a single rhinoceros bearing a single horn.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: (repeating the words, as if to understand better) On two occasions a single rhinoceros ...

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: (doing the same) Bearing a single horn ...

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: ... or you may have seen on two occasions a single rhinoceros with two horns.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (repeating the words) A single rhinoceros with two horns on two occasions ...

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: Exactly. Or again, you may have seen one rhinoceros, with one horn; and then another also with a single horn.

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: (from window) Ha, ha.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: Or again, an initial rhinoceros with two· horns, followed by a second with two horns ...

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: That's true. ..

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: Now, if you had seen ...

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: If we'd seen ...

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Yes, if we'd seen ...

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: if on the first occasion you had seen a rhinoceros with two horns ...

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: With– two horns ...

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: And on the second occasion, a rhinoceros with one horn ...

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: With one horn ...

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: That wouldn't be conclusive either.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Even that wouldn't be conclusive.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: Why not?

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: Oh, I don't get it at all.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: Shoo! Shoo!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The GROCER's WIFE shrugs her shoulders and withdraws from her window.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: For it is possible that since its first appearance, the rhinoceros may have lost one of its horns, and that the first and second transit were still made by a single beast.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I see; but ...

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (interrupting BERENGER) Don't interrupt!

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: It may also be that two rhinoceroses both with two horns may each have lost a horn.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: That is possible.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: Yes, that's possible.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: Why not?

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: Yes, but in any case ...

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: (to BERENGER) Don't interrupt.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: If you could prove that on the first occasion you saw a rhinoceros with one horn, either Asian or African . . .

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Asian or African ...

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: And on the second occasion a rhinoceros with two horns ...

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: One with two ...

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: No matter whether African or Asian ...

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: African or Asian ...

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: ... we could then conclude that we were dealing with two different rhinoceroses, for it is hardly likely that a second horn could grow sufficiently in a space of a few minutes to be visible on the nose of a rhinoceros.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: It's hardly likely.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (enchanted with his discourse) That would imply one rhinoceros either Asian or African ... .

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Asian or African .. .

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: ... and one rhinoceros either African or Asian .

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: African or Asian .

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: Er ... yes.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: For good logic cannot entertain the possibility that the same creature be born in two places at the same time ...

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Or even successively.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to OLD GENTLEMAN) Which was to be proved.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (to LOGICIAN) That seems clear enough, but it doesn't answer the question.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (to BERENGER, with a knowledgeable smile) Obviously; my dear sir, but now the problem is correctly posed.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: It's quite logical. Quite logical.

script.speaker: Logician
script.text: (raising his hat) Good-bye, gentlemen.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He retires, going out left followed by the OLD GENTLEMAN.

script.speaker: Old Gentleman
script.text: Good-bye, gentlemen.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He raises his hat and follows the LOGICIAN out.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: Well, it may be logical …

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: At this moment the HOUSEWIFE comes out of the cafe in deep mourning, and carrying a ho; she is followed by DAISY and the WAITRESS as if for a funeral. The cortege moves towards the right exit.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: ... it may be. logical, but are we going to stand for our cats being run down under our very eyes by one-horned rhinoceroses or two, whether they're Asian or African?

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He indicates with a theatrical gesture the procession which is just leaving.

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: He's absolutely right! We're not standing for our cats being run down by rhinoceroses or anything else!

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: We're not going to stand for it!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: sticking her head round the shop door, to her husband

script.speaker: Grocer's Wife
script.text: Are you coming in? The customers will be here any minute.

script.speaker: Grocer
script.text: · (moving to the shop) No, we're not standing for it.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I should never have quarrelled with Jean! (To the PROPRIETOR:) Get me a brandy! A double!

script.speaker: Proprietor
script.text: Coming up ! (He goes into the cafe for the brandy.)

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: (alone) I never should have quarrelled with Jean. I shouldn't have got into such a rage!

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: The PROPRIETOR comes out carrying a large glass of brandy.

script.speaker: Berenger
script.text: I feel too upset to go to the museum. I'll cultivate my mind some other time.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: He takes the glass of brandy and drinks it.

script.speaker: Stage

SCENE ONE: A GOVERNMENT OFFICE

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: A government office, or legal journal. Upstage center, a large double door, above which a notice reads: 'Chef du Service14. Up-stage left, near to the Head of the Department's door, stands DAISY'S little table with a typewriter. By the left wall stands another table on which the time sheets are placed, which the employees sign on arrival. In the foreground, a table with two chairs. On the table: printing proofs, an inkwell, pens; this is the table where BOTARD and BERENGER work. Near to the right wall, another bigger, rectangular table, also covered with papers, proofs, etc. Two more chairs stand at each end of this table-more elegant and imposing chairs: This is the table of DUDARD and MR. BOEUF. DUDARD will sit on the chair next to the wall, the other employees facing him. He acts as Deputy-Head. Between the up-stage door and the right wall, there is a window. It is preferable to have simply a window frame in front of the stage, facing the auditorium. There is a coat rack. On the walls are rows of books and dusty documents. There are signs: 'Jurisprudence','Codes'; on the right-hand wall which can be slightly on an angle, the signs read: 'Le Journal Officiel', 'Lois fiscales'. Above the Head of the Department's door a clock registers three minutes past nine. When the curtain rises, DUDARD is standing near his chair, his right profile to the auditorium; on the other side of the desk, left profile to the auditorium, is BOTARD; between them, also near to the desk, facing the auditorium, stands the Head of the Department; DAISY is near to the Chief, a little up-stage of him. She holds some sheets of typing paper. On the table round which the three characters stand, a large open newspaper lies on the printing proofs. When the curtain rises the characters remain fixed for a few seconds in position for the first line of dialogue. They make a tableau vivant. The same effect marks the beginning of the first act. The Head of the Department is about forty, very smartly dressed: dark suit, a rosette of the Legion of Honour, starched collar, black tie, large brown moustache. He is MR. PAPILLON. DUDARD, thirty-five years old; grey suit; he wears black lustrine sleeves to protect his coat. He may wear spectacles. He is a quite tall, young employee with a future: If the·Department Head became the Assistant Director he would take his place: BOTARD does not like him.

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: BOTARD: former schoolteacher; short, he has a proud air, and wears a little white moustache; a brisk sixty-year-old: (he knows everything, understands everything, judges everything). He wears a· Basque beret, and wears a long grey blouse during, working hours; spectacles on a longish nose; a pencil behind his ear; he also wears protective sleeves at work. DAISY, a young blonde. Later, MRS. BOEUF; a woman of some forty to fifty years old, tearful, and breathless. As the curtain rises, the characters therefore are standing motion-less around the table, right; the-Chief with index finger pointing to the newspaper; DUDARD, with his hand extended in BOTARDs direction, seems to be saying: 'so you see!’ BOTARD, hands in the

script.speaker: Stage
script.text: pocket of his blouse, wears an incredulous smile and seems to say: 'You won't take me in.' DAISY, with her typing paper in·her hand seems, from her look, to be supporting DUDARD. After a few brief seconds, BOTARD starts the attack.

script.speaker: Botard
script.text: It's all a lot of made-up nonsense.

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: But I saw it, I saw the rhinoceros!

script.speaker: Dudard
script.text: It's in the paper, in black and white, you can't deny that.

script.speaker: Botard
script.text: (with an air of the greatest scorn) Pfff!

script.speaker: Dudard
script.text: It's all here; it's down here in the dead cats column! Read it for yourself, Chief

script.speaker: Papillon
script.text: 'Yesterday, just before lunch time, in the church square of our town, a cat was trampled to death by a pachyderm15.'

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: It wasn't exactly in the church square.

script.speaker: Papillon
script.text: That's all it says. No other details.

script.speaker: Botard
script.text: Pfff!

script.speaker: Dudard
script.text: Well, that's clear enough.

script.speaker: Botard
script.text: I never believe journalists. They're all liars. I don't need them to tell me what to think; I believe what I see with my own eyes. Speaking as a former teacher, I like things to be precise, scientifically valid. I've got a methodical mind.

script.speaker: Dudard
script.text: What's a methodical mind got to do with it?

script.speaker: Daisy
script.text: (to BOTARD) I think it's stated very precisely, Mr. Botard.

script.speaker: Botard
script.text: You call that precise? And what, pray, does it mean by a pachyderm? What does the editor of a dead cats column understand about a pachyderm? He doesn't say. And what does he mean by a cat?

script.speaker: Dudard
script.text: Everybody knows what a cat is.

script.speaker: Botard
script.text: Does it concern a male cat or a female? What breed was it? And what color? I hate systemic racism, it’s something I feel very strongly about.

script.speaker: Dudard
script.text: What has the color got to do with it, Mr. Botard? It's quite beside the point. elephants, rhinoceroses, and hippopotamuses

script.speaker: Botard
script.text: It's not an issue to be dismissed lightly, Mr. Dudard. The course of history has shown that racial prejudice ...

script.speaker: Dudard
script.text: I tell you it doesn't enter into it.

script.speaker: Botard
script.text: I'm not so sure.

script.speaker: Papillon
